findings.title: Skill-resource allowlist documentation omits the reviewed ancestor repository scope
findings.description: The operational documentation says resource/skill/read permits only the registered project and fixed global roots. The implemented M240 contract additionally permits precise ancestor .agents/skills directories up to the nearest actual non-symlink Git worktree root. The restrictive implementation is correct and covered, but the documented exhaustive allowlist is outdated and can mislead an operator investigating why an ancestor skill is readable.
evidence: Read the current read_skill root construction, nearest-.git stop, descriptor containment and forbidden-root checks.

tests/deploy/test_workspace_resources.py::ResourceFilesystemTests.test_catalog_ancestor_skill_is_limited_to_nearest_git_worktree checks the ancestor skill succeeds while outside and non-skill siblings fail.
No behavior or production change was made during review.
findings.recommendation: Update the exact allowlist description to include only repository-bound ancestor .agents/skills, retaining the no-symlink, catalog-selection and protected-root restrictions. Do not broaden implementation access.

delegatedReviewer: root; same-round full3-tooling-protocol report covers five named root fixtures and the three Go lock/entry files. Those eight are excluded from personal coverage.

baseline.method: Parent explicitly authorized reuse of the previous complete semantic review for unchanged files, coupled to current repair/call-chain impact review. The full2 reviewer confirmed the 12 finalSourceFiles in full2-deploy-fixes.json are all post-full2 deploy/test changes. Every changed executable and regression assertion was reread here; unchanged tests were reviewed for their current consumers, assertion families and fixture substitution boundaries against the newly reread production implementation. This is not a claim that all unchanged test bodies were mechanically reread in this round.

method: Verified the official frozen-source snapshot with scripts/snapshot.mjs at audit start and end. All 154 scope file hashes also match the pre-audit inventory, so pre-freeze read-only preparation remains bound to this source.

Read all production deployment Python/shell/documentation and local Go tests in full, except the three explicitly root-delegated Go lock/entry files. Followed actual privilege, call, state, failure, durability and recovery contracts rather than limiting inspection to changed lines.

Reread all full2 changes and their affected production callers: waitid WNOWAIT ownership through group/descendant cleanup in supervisor, ordinary Git queries and prepared ref transactions; HSTS target validation and public-to-internal migration; historical PID birth-identity checks; operational upgrade and recovery prose.

Fully reread root HTTPS transaction fixture plus ordinary HTTPS/rendering/guidance/port fixtures, native shutdown/process fixtures, workspace commit/index/resources, complete history-copy/compaction/attachment tests, runbook probe, local MCP stdio probe and root toolchain subclass. Verified real assertion targets and the explicit boundaries where OS, TLS service or process behavior is substituted.

For unchanged remaining test modules, reused full2 whole-body semantic evidence and reviewed per-file imports, production call relationships, all assertion/test identities and changed-path relevance. The structural extraction is only a navigation record, not a replacement claimed as new whole-body review. Full-body and baseline-reused lists are separate.
No source modification, production command, paid turn, external MCP tool, whole-suite execution, commit or deployment occurred during this audit.

semanticChecks.result: Leader identity remains unreaped through every killpg; already-reaped leaders refuse cleanup. Final wait follows all adopted-child cleanup. Git transaction keeps exclusive child ownership; unknown cleanup retains its index lock. Linux fixtures assert real child exit plus owned-leader signaling, without claiming actual forced PID reuse.

Explicit HSTS validity precedes staging or credentials; internal target clears inherited HSTS and preserves recovery bytes. Before/after units, service active/enabled choices, DNS/provided material, client identity and terminal journaling retain independent proofs. TLS proof remains host/SNI/nonce-bound with bounded resolution and response size.

Copies retain an independent native target header/ID/provider and require a still-empty exact target. Source bytes, inode, hash, timestamp and writer locks are checked before and after copying. Compacted parallel metadata and inherited-history boundaries are explicit; opaque/uninspectable data never proves absence or authorizes destructive cleanup.

Ordinary launch checks fixed identity/no capabilities/no_new_privs; full root remains intentional opt-in. External server authorization rejects service ancestry. Shared auth transfers only while stopped with private inode-bound recovery; it does not share history. Provider, DNS, proxy and account material remain separately bounded and redacted.

Exact canonical UTF-8-plus-newline persistence limits precede generation/profile writes. Compact receipts preserve identity and reread contract. Toolchain generation spec binds current versions, architecture and official hashes; legacy cache stays retained and cannot be silently selected. Interrupted publication is verified and resynced before reuse.

Receipt/spool locks and capacity remain distinct; unknown execution is never replayed or rewritten as not_sent. Final published success is not compensated because the last durability report fails. Stopped recovery preserves schema, identities, root authorization, authentication guard and service enablement choices.

No-follow descriptors, exact revisions, inode capture and no-replace publication preserve conflicting files. Prepared Git transactions start no sibling helper while owning ref locks. Worktree retire is clean-only, archives bytes and frees only its bound active slot; search and incomplete snapshots report conservative limits.

Official source/hash binding, isolated fetch/offline build, stopped producer import, exact managed units/sudo and cgroup route membership remain enforced. Per-instance proxy optionality, direct-domain routing, fixed download targets and retained old core/config rollback remain unchanged.

limitations: This is source and fixture audit, not a new test run. Prior directed Windows/Linux/root test evidence is referenced only for its exact recorded source and boundary.

Real systemd boot, public TLS issuance/renewal, paid model providers and real MCP credentials are not established by substituted-root fixtures. The installed crtest linux_isolation and linux_native_boundary probes have not been rerun in this audit.
The DNS dependency checksum lock is delegated for structural integrity and closed-build verification; neither review claims that every vendored third-party implementation was source-audited.
No real PID reuse or unrelated process signaling was induced. Synthetic identity reuse and real isolated subprocess ownership fixtures establish the repaired code path only.
One actionable documentation finding remains; this report is not a clean audit.
